raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Enable decode-side prefix KV reuse for hybrid attention models in PD serving, supporting **EAGLE/MTP (top-k 1) and DFLASH (DFlash2)**. Shared-prefix requests reuse KV on the decode worker instead of allocating and transferring a separate copy for every request.

This reduces KV capacity pressure and transfer volume, allowing more requests to decode concurrently. Recurrent state remains request-local: each request uses its own full-prompt state received from prefill, including when shared prefixes have different suffixes.

## Modifications

- Decouple prefix KV matching from Mamba/KDA checkpoints while keeping recurrent-state ownership and release request-local.
- Preserve EAGLE bigram-key semantics at prefix boundaries and integrate DFLASH with its existing verification and recurrent-state update paths.
- Account for running and in-flight PD requests when budgeting persistent and speculative state.

Enabled through the existing `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` option, using Python TreeCore. Hybrid speculative use supports EAGLE/MTP (top-k 1) and DFLASH with NIXL, without target-model sliding-window attention; unsupported cache/session combinations are rejected.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated GLM-5.3-Flash on 8 × H200 with TP4/EP4 on both P and D. Full GSM8K evaluation (1,314 examples, 5-shot, BF16 recurrent state) achieved:

| Configuration | Mean GSM8K accuracy (two runs) |
| --- | ---: |
| MTP516 + D radix cache | **95.66%** |
| DFlash2 block8 + D radix cache | **95.81%** |

Both configurations include the independent KDA tracking dtype fix in #44886.

- Shared-prefix, isolated-prefix, and concurrent requests returned the expected answers, including requests with different suffixes. D-side prefix hits were confirmed independently of P-side caching.
- **106 CPU regression tests passed**, covering KV-only matching, state isolation/release, draft-KV boundary keys, and state budgeting. Pre-commit checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On a long shared-prefix workload, decode-side radix caching improves output throughput by **25.8% with MTP516** and **77.4% with DFlash2 block8**. TTFT P50 falls by **69.1%** and **85.0%**, respectively, as prefix KV reuse relieves decode KV capacity pressure and request admission queuing.

**Configuration:** GLM-5.3-Flash, 8 × H200 (P: GPUs 0–3; D: GPUs 4–7), TP4/EP4, FP8 target KV and BF16 recurrent state. MTP uses MTP112 on P and MTP516 on D; DFlash2 uses block8 on both workers with BF16 draft KV. D uses ReplaySSM speculative state, and P-side caching stays enabled. All configurations use the same code and common serving settings, including memory fractions and request limits. Each OFF/ON pair differs only in D-side radix caching.

**Workload:** C32, 1K output, 252K shared prefix + 4K unique suffix (~273K actual input tokens per request). Results are medians of three runs after warmup; all 512 requests per run succeeded in every configuration.

### EAGLE/MTP (MTP516)

| Metric | D radix OFF | D radix ON |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 2,785.46 | 3,505.37 |
| TTFT P50 (s) | 5.84 | 1.81 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 5.26 | 6.29 |
| TPOT P50 (ms) | 4.68 | 5.61 |
| D target KV capacity (tokens) | 4,745,728 | 4,745,728 |

### DFLASH (DFlash2 block8)

| Metric | D radix OFF | D radix ON |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 1,788.97 | 3,174.52 |
| TTFT P50 (s) | 12.31 | 1.85 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 4.87 | 6.95 |
| TPOT P50 (ms) | 3.16 | 4.73 |
| D target KV capacity (tokens) | 2,843,904 | 2,843,904 |

Both algorithms achieve higher throughput and lower TTFT with prefix KV reuse, while TPOT increases, likely due to larger active decode batches. With radix caching enabled, MTP516 delivers 3,505.37 tok/s versus 3,174.52 tok/s for DFlash2 block8 on this workload.

## Reproduction commands

Run P, D, and the router in separate terminals with the SGLang environment activated. The commands below reproduce the MTP configuration: P112 on GPUs 0–3 and D516 on GPUs 4–7. Use the default Triton MoE configurations (`SGLANG_MOE_CONFIG_DIR` unset).

### Prefill worker

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python \
SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ENGINE_INIT_TIMEOUT=300 \
SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=UCX \
UCX_NET_DEVICES=lo \
UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,self,sm \
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
sglang serve \
  --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name llm \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --ep-size 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend triton \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \
  --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton \
  --linear-attn-decode-backend triton \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 8192 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 1 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2 \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl \
  --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 \
  --enable-request-time-stats-logging \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --tokenizer-worker-num 4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 31000 \
  --nccl-port 29500
```

### Decode worker

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \
SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python \
SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ENGINE_INIT_TIMEOUT=300 \
SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=UCX \
UCX_NET_DEVICES=lo \
UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,self,sm \
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
sglang serve \
  --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name llm \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --ep-size 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend triton \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \
  --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton \
  --linear-attn-decode-backend triton \
  --linear-attn-verify-backend triton \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.86 \
  --max-mamba-cache-size 390 \
  --max-running-requests 124 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 124 \
  --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 24 32 48 64 80 88 96 104 112 116 120 124 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --enable-linear-replayssm-spec \
  --disaggregation-mode decode \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl \
  --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache \
  --disaggregation-decode-extra-slots 6 \
  --enable-request-time-stats-logging \
  --log-level info \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --tokenizer-worker-num 4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 32000 \
  --nccl-port 29501
```

### Router

```bash
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
python -m sglang_router.launch_router \
  --pd-disaggregation \
  --mini-lb \
  --prefill http://127.0.0.1:31000 8998 \
  --decode http://127.0.0.1:32000 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8090
```

### DFlash2 block8

To reproduce the DFlash2 results, replace the four EAGLE speculative options in **both** worker commands with the following options. Use the same DFlash2 block8 checkpoint on P and D; keep the remaining flags and router command unchanged.

```bash
--speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
--speculative-draft-model-path /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2 \
--speculative-dflash-block-size 8 \
--speculative-draft-attention-backend fa3 \
--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype bfloat16
```

For the MTP radix-disabled baseline, omit `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` from the decode command.

### GSM8K accuracy

Use the same evaluation command for MTP516 and DFlash2 block8: 5-shot, 8 threads, two repeats.

```bash
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
python -u -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8090 \
  --api chat \
  --model llm \
  --eval-name gsm8k \
  --gsm8k-data-path /path/to/gsm8k/test.jsonl \
  --num-examples 1314 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --num-threads 8 \
  --repeat 2 \
  --max-tokens 4096 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"low"}'
```

### C32 throughput

Run each configuration from a separate results directory. The following runs three rounds of 512 requests at C32, with a 252K shared prefix, 4K unique suffix, and 1K output. Each round clears the cache before 10 warmup requests; report the median throughput across the three rounds. Run this separately from accuracy evaluation.

```bash
for round in 1 2 3; do
  curl --noproxy 127.0.0.1 -fsS \
    --connect-timeout 10 \
    --max-time 300 \
    -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/flush_cache > /dev/null || break

  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" \
  SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=0 \
  NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
  no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
  python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
    --model /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash \
    --served-model-name llm \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port 8090 \
    --backend sglang \
    --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
    --num-prompts 512 \
    --gsp-num-groups 1 \
    --gsp-prompts-per-group 512 \
    --gsp-system-prompt-len 258048 \
    --gsp-question-len 4096 \
    --gsp-output-len 1024 \
    --gsp-range-ratio 1.0 \
    --request-rate inf \
    --max-concurrency 32 \
    --warmup-requests 10 \
    --temperature 0.0 \
    --seed 42 \
    --cache-report \
    --output-details \
    --output-file "c32_round${round}.jsonl" || break
done
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

Scope is required and may be any module or model name, with unrestricted letter case (letters, numbers, dots, underscores, slashes, or hyphens). Hardware is optional; use a single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend. Reverts must use GitHub's default format: Revert "original title". Use one space between fields and after the colon, with a non-empty title and no leading or trailing whitespace. Examples: "[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing", "[Feat] qwen3: Add model support", "[Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance".
Edit the title; the check reruns on its own.

Hi @Jzz1943, a sizing note from #44015 that touches the `_handle_max_mamba_cache` change here.

In KV-only decode mode this PR budgets the verify scratch for running plus in-transfer requests (`capped_reqs = min(...) + self._mamba_prealloc_requests()` in both spec-state branches). That matches what `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool` allocates on main today (`size + pre_alloc_size` rows). But in-transfer requests never run `target_verify`, and `intermediate_ssm` / `intermediate_conv_window` are indexed by batch row (`build_verify_intermediate_state_indices` over `req_to_token_pool.size`), so those rows are never used. #44015 stops allocating them in the default configuration (no ReplaySSM-spec, no `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC`). With both PRs in, the two terms would reserve `pre_alloc_size` rows that are never allocated, and the KV pool would come out smaller than it needs to be.

The other prealloc terms look right to me: in-transfer requests do hold a persistent Mamba slot (`_mamba_running_request_capacity`), and GDN's ReplaySSM ring is keyed by `req_pool_idx` (`replay_req_slots`).

Whichever merges second can fix it: if #44015 goes first, the term can be dropped here; if this PR goes first, I'll remove it in #44015.

@QNan0513 Thanks for catching this. Agreed—the default verify scratch only needs running-batch rows. Since #44015 is still open and main still allocates size + pre_alloc_size, I’ve retained the matching budget for now. Whichever PR merges second can align the scratch budget and allocation, while keeping transfer-slot reserves for persistent state and request-indexed rings.

Hi @Jzz1943, a sizing note from #44015 that touches the `_handle_max_mamba_cache` change here.

In KV-only decode mode this PR budgets the verify scratch for running plus in-transfer requests (`capped_reqs = min(...) + self._mamba_prealloc_requests()` in both spec-state branches). That matches what `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool` allocates on main today (`size + pre_alloc_size` rows). But in-transfer requests never run `target_verify`, and `intermediate_ssm` / `intermediate_conv_window` are indexed by batch row (`build_verify_intermediate_state_indices` over `req_to_token_pool.size`), so those rows are never used. #44015 stops allocating them in the default configuration (no ReplaySSM-spec, no `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC`). With both PRs in, the two terms would reserve `pre_alloc_size` rows that are never allocated, and the KV pool would come out smaller than it needs to be.

The other prealloc terms look right to me: in-transfer requests do hold a persistent Mamba slot (`_mamba_running_request_capacity`), and GDN's ReplaySSM ring is keyed by `req_pool_idx` (`replay_req_slots`).

Whichever merges second can fix it: if #44015 goes first, the term can be dropped here; if this PR goes first, I'll remove it in #44015.

@QNan0513 Thanks for catching this. Agreed—the default verify scratch only needs running-batch rows. Since #44015 is still open and main still allocates size + pre_alloc_size, I’ve retained the matching budget for now. Whichever PR merges second can align the scratch budget and allocation, while keeping transfer-slot reserves for persistent state and request-indexed rings.
